Planning Statement – Proposed Front Porch
This application seeks planning permission for the construction of a modest front porch at 41 Beardsfield E13 0LD.
The proposed development would ordinarily fall within the scope of permitted development rights under Schedule 2, Part 1, Class D of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended). However, due to a restrictive covenant contained within the Third Schedule (Covenant 3) of the original freehold title dated 1998, the applicant is submitting this application to obtain formal consent.

Description of Development
The proposed porch will have maximum external dimensions of approximately 1.48 metres in depth and 2.00 metres in width, resulting in a footprint of under 3 square metres. The maximum height will be approximately 2.70 metres at the highest point, including an existing concrete foundation of approximately 0.12 metres.
The structure will be positioned at the front of the property, enclosing the existing entrance area where to current door will be maintained. 

Design and Materials
The porch will be constructed primarily from white uPVC, incorporating glazed panels and windows to ensure a light and visually unobtrusive appearance. The roof will be tiled in red to match as far as possible the existing roof of the dwelling, ensuring visual continuity with the surrounding area.

Impact on the Character of the Area
Given its modest scale and sympathetic design, the proposed porch will appear as a subordinate addition to the existing dwelling. The materials and roof finish have been selected to complement the host property, and the development will not appear incongruous within the street scene.
Porches of similar size and design are common features in residential areas and do not detract from the character or appearance of properties.

Impact on Neighbouring Amenity
Due to its limited size, height, and position at the front of the property, the proposed porch will not result in any material loss of light, outlook, or privacy to neighbouring properties. The development is considered to have a negligible impact on residential amenity.

Highways and Access
The proposal does not alter the existing access arrangements to the property and will not impact highway safety or visibility.

Conclusion
The proposed development is modest in scale, appropriate in design, and would normally be considered permitted development. It will not result in harm to the character of the area or neighbouring amenity. The application is therefore respectfully submitted for approval.
